historic_survey.note: Listed as San Francisco Landmark No. 255 and named among the neighbourhood's historic school buildings; its tower is domed in mosaic tile.

historical_record.description: The first Mission High School was completed on land formerly owned by the Jewish Cemetery Association — a monumental Renaissance Revival building by Charles I. Havens, and the first public comprehensive high school in San Francisco. A figure caption in the same statement dates it 1897.
The school survived the earthquake and fire and overlooked the refugee camp in Mission Park.

building.name: Mission High School
building.completed_conflict: The statement dates Mission High School to a two-phased construction in 1925 and 1927 in one passage and to 1926 in another; Planning's historic resource survey records 1926 and the assessor's roll 1900.
